one_sentence_story: Nearly fifteen years after a brainstem stroke left Cathy Hutchinson unable to speak or move, a baby-aspirin-sized chip inside her brain's movement strip translated her imagined arm motions into a real silver robotic arm so she could lift a coffee bottle and take a sip on her own.
so_what_for_you: Even after fifteen years of total paralysis, your brain's movement strip keeps its reach-and-grasp blueprint alive — proving human motor intention endures and can bypass broken nerve highways.
